examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
A queue is FIFO. Circular-array conventions decide whether front/rear name occupied slots or next positions. Index equality alone cannot distinguish empty from full if all slots are used; a count, bit or reserved slot is needed. A deque permits both-end operations and is a different interface. With two stacks, occasional expensive transfers can still give constant amortized queue operations.

**Key relationship:** Next circular index=(current+1) mod capacity

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Write the index convention.
2. Distinguish capacity from array length.
3. Trace wraparound and full/empty conditions.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A queue removes in arrival order. In a circular implementation, define whether front/rear point to occupied cells or the next insertion cell. Full and empty can share index equality unless a count, extra bit, or unused slot distinguishes them. Capacity includes entries retained during transfers.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A circular queue has an array of size 8 and reserves one slot to distinguish full from empty. What is its maximum occupancy?

**Answer: 7.** With one slot deliberately unused, at most 8−1=7 entries can be stored. Under the next-insertion rear convention, full is (rear+1) mod8=front.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Other implementations use every array position with an explicit count. The one-empty-slot formula is not universal.

If front=rear means empty, the same equality cannot also mean full without extra state.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A circular array of size 10 reserves one slot. Queue capacity?

- **A.** 9
- **B.** 10
- **C.** 11
- **D.** 8

**Answer: A.** The unused slot distinguishes full from empty, leaving 10−1=9 usable entries.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** FIFO removes earliest retained arrival
- **B.** Circular indices wrap modulo array size
- **C.** Using every slot requires a way to distinguish full from empty
- **D.** Every individual two-stack dequeue is worst-case O(1)

**Answer: A, B, C.** A transfer can take linear time for one dequeue even though the amortized cost is constant.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

An eight-slot ring has front=6 and next-insertion rear=2. Using one reserved slot, current occupancy?



**Answer: 4.** Occupancy=(rear−front+8) mod8=(2−6+8) mod8=4.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q59 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/queues?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Stacks and expression evaluation. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. After loading, S from bottom to top is [1,5,7,8,9,2], and Q from front to rear is [1,5,7,8,9,2].
2. Operations III–VI remove stack elements 2,9 and queue elements 1,5. S=[1,5,7,8], Q=[7,8,9,2]. Operations VII–VIII transfer all four queue elements onto S, producing [1,5,7,8,7,8,9,2].
3. Operations IX–X pop 2 then 9, leaving **8** at the top.

#### GATE 2026 CS2 · Q50 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/queues?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Stacks and expression evaluation. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. A puts [1,3,4] into S and [2,5] into Q. Popping then dequeueing gives 4,3,1,2,5.
2. B puts [3,4] into S and [1,2,5] into Q, producing the same result.
3. C starts its output with 5 and D starts with 3, so neither matches. Select **A,B**.
